# The quarnet

A quarnet was a unit of dry volume used in the grain trade of the lower river ports. One
quarnet equalled four bushels and two pecks. Three quarnets made a load, and a load was the
quantity a single cart was assumed to carry to market.

The unit fell out of use when the ports standardised on metric measures. It survives only in
port ledgers and in the phrase "a quarnet short", which meant a delivery that had lost volume
in transit.
